findings.claim: The zero-durable-write proof has an unmonitored hole: the `/api/config/persistence` route fulfills HTTP 204 (success) for every method without recording non-GET requests, so a durable write through that endpoint would be silently accepted and the final `expect(durableSettingsWrites).toEqual([])` would still pass.
findings.evidence: Hunk: `await page.route(/\/api\/config\/persistence(?:\?.*)?$/, async (route) => { await route.fulfill({ status: 204 }); });` — contrast with the settings-namespace route which records and 409-rejects all non-GET requests. Constraint `keyboard-and-draft-preservation` requires "no durable write occurs" validated by "zero-write assertions"; iteration 3 of the refinement log claims route coverage was made fail-closed, but this endpoint (named 'persistence') remains open to unrecorded writes.
findings.suggested_fix: Record non-GET requests in `durableSettingsWrites` (or a sibling array) inside the `/api/config/persistence` handler and reject them with a non-2xx status, matching the fail-closed pattern used for the settings namespace.

findings.claim: The exact-36rem state assertion is subpixel-flaky: the width poll tolerates ±0.5px (`toBeCloseTo(width, 0)`) at exactly the value where the container query flips, so a measured content box of e.g. 575.6px passes the poll but yields one track where the test expects two.
findings.evidence: `setContentBoxWidth` asserts `expect.poll(() => contentBoxWidth(locator)).toBeCloseTo(width, 0)` (|diff| < 0.5), then the test calls `await setContentBoxWidth(providerList, boundary); expect(await computedTrackCount(grid)).toBe(2);`. `contentBoxWidth` derives from integer `clientWidth` minus parsed float padding, so fractional rounding from zoom/DPI/scrollbar environments can land inside the tolerance band but below the 36rem flip point.
findings.suggested_fix: For the exact-boundary state, poll with a strict equality on the rounded content-box width (e.g. assert `Math.round(width) === boundary` after setting) or offset the exact-boundary check by a subpixel-safe epsilon that still satisfies the at-or-above spec clause deterministically.

findings.claim: The accepted spec scenario requires every visible provider control to remain "fully reachable and operable by keyboard", but the browser contract only proves reachability, focus visibility, and geometry — no control is ever operated via keyboard.
findings.evidence: spec.md scenario: "- **AND** each visible provider control remains fully reachable and operable by keyboard". In `provider-settings-responsive.spec.ts`, `expectKeyboardPath` only presses Tab and asserts focus/style; `baseUrl.fill(dirtyValue)` is a programmatic fill, and no Space/Enter/typing interaction exercises the Enable switch, reveal button, Protocol select, or Default Model combobox.
findings.suggested_fix: Add keyboard-operation assertions (e.g. Space toggles Enable and preserves the dirty Base URL, Enter/Space on reveal toggles visibility, typing into Base URL updates the draft) or narrow the scenario wording to match the reachable-with-visible-focus evidence.

findings.claim: The new registry entry omits `finalized_at`, which every sibling entry in the same object carries; if the registry schema requires that field per entry, the manifest/schema-validation termination condition cannot pass.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk: the added `fix-provider-settings-panel-width-responsiveness` entry has only `path`, `artifact_type`, `content_type`, `updated_at`, while the visible sibling entries (e.g. the 2026-08-23 entry directly above) all include `finalized_at`. Termination conditions require "Manifest, constraints, referenced files, iteration history, strict OpenSpec, and diff integrity validate."
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm against the registry schema whether `finalized_at` is optional for in-flight refinements; if required, either add it on finalization before claiming validation, or record the schema's optionality explicitly in the artifact evidence.

findings.claim: `expectKeyboardPath` permanently clobbers any pre-existing `tabindex` on `document.body` because cleanup unconditionally calls `removeAttribute("tabindex")` rather than restoring the prior value.
findings.evidence: `page.evaluate(() => { document.body.tabIndex = -1; document.body.focus(); })` followed by `finally { await page.evaluate(() => document.body.removeAttribute("tabindex")); }` — if the shell ever sets a body tabindex, this test silently removes it for the remainder of the session.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the original attribute (`document.body.getAttribute("tabindex")`) and restore it in the `finally` block, mirroring the pattern already used for `originalStyle` on the provider list.
